findings.location: Definition, lines 27–47 (inline item links at lines 28–30, 33–34, and 44–45)
findings.evidence: The complete Definition embeds links to def-banach-space, def-metric-topology, bounded-operator targets, and def-operator-norm. The links interrupt the definition and are not placed in an immediately following Definition references section. Move them after the complete definition while preserving its hypotheses and derivative condition.

The complete norm claim embeds links to the real and complex norm definitions and has no following Statement references section. Move the links after the complete statement without removing the scalar-field qualification.

The explanatory claim that the kernel and image are subspaces and characterize injectivity ends with an inline link to thm-linear-kernel-image-and-injectivity inside the Definition. Move the supplier link after the complete Definition.
The definition's properties of S-perp contain inline links to def-linear-subspace and cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm. Move both links after the complete Definition.
The pairwise-orthogonality hypothesis is interrupted by an inline link to its definition, and no following Statement references section is present. Move the link after the complete statement.

The definition contains malformed title insertions including “is the function space of The vector space”, “the finite sum of Finite sums”, and “That ... is a norm in the sense of A norm ... is proved in Cauchy-Schwarz”. The surrounding function-space and n=0/metric-scope prose is also grammatically broken. Restore coherent mathematical prose and preserve the stated n=0 versus n>=1 distinction.

Citation-title fragments remain inside the complete definition, including “(Real and imaginary parts, complex conjugation, and modulus)”, “in the sense of Real and complex inner product spaces”, and “the published The norm”. Replace these with plain mathematical wording while preserving the field, conjugation, inner-product axioms, and induced-length clauses; the targets are already listed after the definition.

The statement retains citation-title text in “(Limits and Cauchy sequences of reals)” and “Together with The reals form a totally ordered field”, making the prose ill formed despite the clear completeness conclusion. Rewrite in mathematical prose and retain the no-choice qualification; the cited targets already follow in Statement references.

Title text leaks into the statement as “as in The Euclidean inner product” and “the published The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality”. The mathematical clauses are identifiable, but this statement prose is ill formed. Replace the title fragments with plain mathematical terms and preserve the exact equality condition and references.

The statement contains title insertions (“finite sums as in Finite sums and finite products”, “(Square roots exist: ...)”, and a repeated “Square roots exist: ...” clause) that make the prose ill formed. State the finite-sum and nonnegative-square-root hypotheses in mathematical terms, retaining the n=0 scope and equality condition; the supplier links already follow in Statement references.

Citation-title fragments remain in the definition, and lines 63–69 contain malformed prose (“Which metric axiom list ... records why” and “not an axiom proves”). Repair the text into complete mathematical statements while preserving the metric axioms and nonnegativity caveat. The assigned consumer reaches this published item through batch 1's def-ip-forward-map-and-solution-classes.
